(Capacity: 9,000) |champion = [[Asheville Championship]] champions |tourney = [[2024 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] |tourney_result = Elite Eight }} {{2023–24 ACC men's basketball standings}} The '''2023–24 Clemson Tigers men's basketball team''' represented [[Clemson University]] during the [[2023–24 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Tigers were led by 14th-year head coach [[Brad Brownell]] and played their home games at [[Littlejohn Coliseum]] in [[Clemson, South Carolina]] as members of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]]. The Tigers began the season with nine straight wins. This included a one-point win over [[2023–24 UAB Blazers men's basketball team|UAB]] and a three-point win over [[2023–24 Davidson Wildcats men's basketball team|Davidson]] to claim the [[Asheville Championship]]. They continued their strong start to the season, upsetting twenty-third ranked [[2023–24 Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball team|Alabama]] in the [[ACC–SEC Challenge]]. They opened the ACC season with a nine-point win at [[2023–24 Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball team|Pittsburgh]]. They debuted in the national rankings at twenty-fourth before their [[Clemson–South Carolina rivalry|rivalry]] game with [[2023–24 South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball team|South Carolina]]. They won that game and their ensuing game against [[2023–24 TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball team|TCU]] for their ninth win of the season. After the win, they achieved their highest ranking during the season of thirteenth. Their first defeat was by two-points against [[2023–24 Memphis Tigers men's basketball team|Memphis]] on December 16, 2023. They won their final two non-conference games to finish their non-conference season 10–1. Their non-conference success did not carry into the start of their ACC season as they lost four of their first five games. A loss to [[2023–24 Miami Hurricanes men's basketball team|Miami (FL)]] and eighth-ranked [[2023–24 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]] dropped them to twenty-first in the rankings. Despite defeating [[2023–24 Boston College Eagles men's basketball team|Boston College]] and losing to [[2023–24 Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball team|Virginia Tech]], the Tigers fell out of the rankings. A double-overtime loss to [[2023–24 Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball team|Georgia Tech]] capped the first five games. The Tigers won five of their next seven games, including only their second ever win at North Carolina. They lost by a point at twelfth-ranked [[2023–24 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]] and also by a point to [[2023–24 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|Virginia]]. They Tigers won four of their last six games including the completion of a season sweep against Pittsburgh and [[2023–24 Florida State Seminoles men's basketball team|Florida State]]. They ended the season with a loss to [[2023–24 Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball team|Wake Forest]]. After the season, [[Ian Schieffelin]] was named ACC Most Improved Player, becoming the second Clemson player to win the award. [[PJ Hall]] was named to the All-ACC First Team. The Tigers finished the season 24–12 and 11–9 in [[2023–24 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]] to finish in a three-way tie for fifth place. As the sixth seed in the [[2024 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]], were defeated by [[2023–24 Boston College Eagles men's basketball team|Boston College]] in the Second Round. They earned an at-large bid to the [[2024 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] and were placed as the sixth-seed in the [[2024 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament#West regional – Los Angeles, California|West]] region. They defeated eleventh-seed [[2023–24 New Mexico Lobos men's basketball team|New Mexico]] in the First Round, third-seed [[2023–24 Baylor Bears men's basketball team|Baylor]] in the Second Round and second-seed [[2023–24 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team|Arizona]] in the Sweet Sixteen. This advanced Clemson to only their second Elite Eight in program history. In the Elite Eight the Tigers lost in a rematch of an early season game against Alabama 89–82 to end their season. ==Previous season== The [[2022–23 Clemson Tigers men's basketball team|Tigers]] finished the [[2022–23 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2022–23 season]] 23–11, 14–6 in [[2022–23 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]], in a three-way tie for third place. As the third seed in the [[2023 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]], they earned a bye into the Quarterfinals where they defeated sixth seed [[2022–23 NC State Wolfpack men's basketball team|NC State]] for the third time during the season. They fell to second seeded [[2022–23 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|Virginia]] in the semifinals. They were not selected for the [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] and were listed as the fourth team out on Selection Sunday. They received a first overall seed in the [[2023 National Invitation Tournament|National Invitation Tournament]].{{cite web|url=https://www.thestate.com/sports/college/acc/clemson-university/article273055365.html|title=Clemson basketball left out of NCAA Tournament, named No. 1 seed for NIT|work=[[The State (newspaper)|The State]]|first=Chapel|last=Fowler|date=March 13, 2023|access-date=April 6, 2023}} Despite being the first seed, and hosting, the Tigers lost to [[2022–23 Morehead State Eagles men's basketball team|Morehead State]] in the first round to end their season. Clemson started the season 6–0 in [[2022–23 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]], for the first time since the ACC was created as a conference. Their previous best was in the [[Clemson Tigers men's basketball, 1990–1999#1996–97|1996–97 season]] when they started 5–0.{{cite web|url=https://apnews.com/article/sports-louisville-cardinals-clemson-tigers-mens-basketball-7642c68f92edefae316801544eaa3d1f|title=Tyson scores 28, Clemson reaches 6-0 in ACC for first time|website=apnews.com|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|date=January 12, 2023|access-date=January 12, 2023}} The Tigers continued their run by defeating [[2022–23 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]] but then lost to [[2022–23 Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball team|Wake Forest]] to end their undefeated run. They won their next two games and were 9–1 at the halfway point of the conference season. This gave the team its best six, seven, eight, nine and ten game starts in conference history.{{cite web|url=https://www.tigernet.com/clemson-basketball/story/tigers-complete-sweep-of-jackets-reach-record-9-1-at-halftime-in-acc-play-21047|title=Tigers complete sweep of Jackets, reach record 9–1 at halftime in ACC play|website=tigernet.com|publisher=TigerNet|first=Brandon|last=Rink|date=January 24, 2023|access-date=January 25, 2023}} The Tigers would set another program record on February 15, 2023, when they defeated [[2022–23 Florida State Seminoles men's basketball team|Florida State]] 94–54 at home. This was the Tigers' widest margin of victory in ACC play, beating the previous record of a 34-point win in 1975.{{cite web|url=https://www.tigernet.com/clemson-basketball/story/tigers-bounce-back-in-blowout-fashion-over-florida-state-21094|title=Tigers bounce back in blowout fashion over Florida State|website=tigernet.com|publisher=TigerNet|first=Brandon|last=Rink|date=February 15, 2023|access-date=February 16, 2023}} ==Offseason== ===Departures=== {|class="wikitable sortable" border="1" style="text-align: center;" ! colspan=8 style="{{CollegePrimaryStyle|Clemson Tigers}}" | Clemson Departures |- align=center {{CollegeSecondaryHeader|team=Clemson Tigers| Name| Number| Pos.| Height| Weight| Year| Hometown|class8=unsortable| Reason for departure}} |- | [[Hunter Tyson]] || 5 || F || 6'8" || 215 || {{sort|4.5|[[File:Redshirt.svg|15px|Redshirt]] Senior}} || [[Monroe, NC]] || Graduated/[[2023 NBA draft]]; selected
